tasks.title: Add cairn task next-id to the planner's allowedTools
tasks.description:
`src/commands/plan.ts` (around line 166) spawns the interactive planning session with:

    '--allowedTools', 'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent',

But `commands/generate-tasks.md:149` requires the planning session to run `cairn task next-id --count <n>` to allocate task IDs. Because that command is not pre-approved, it prompts the user mid-generation in every project — friction sitting directly on the critical path of the core workflow.

Add a rule pre-approving `cairn task next-id` (prefix form, e.g. `Bash(cairn task next-id:*)`).

SCOPE STRICTLY to `next-id`. Do not add other `cairn task` subcommands, do not add git rules, and do not otherwise widen the planner — interactive prompt fatigue in general is deliberately NOT this round's target. Note that task #80 adds deny rules for the five MUTATING `cairn task` subcommands; `next-id` is deliberately excluded from those denies, and deny would beat this allow if the two ever overlapped.

TDD against test/commands/plan.test.ts: assert the emitted allowedTools string, then implement.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.
tasks.notes:
# Task #81 — Add `cairn task next-id` to the planner's allowedTools

## What changed

- `src/commands/plan.ts:166` — `--allowedTools` value changed from
  `Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent` to
  `Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent,Bash(cairn task next-id:*)`.
- `test/commands/plan.test.ts` — updated the existing exact-string assertion
  (`spawns claude with --allowedTools including Agent for slash command
  support`) to expect the new string, and added a new test (`pre-approves
  cairn task next-id so ID allocation does not prompt mid-generation`) that
  additionally asserts scope: no `Bash(cairn task:*)` blanket grant and no
  grant for any of the five mutating subcommands (start/complete/note/
  set-status/add).

## TDD sequence

1. Edited the test file first to assert the new allowedTools string — ran
   `bun test test/commands/plan.test.ts`, confirmed both assertions failed
   (red): received `Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent` (old value, no next-id
   grant).
2. Made the one-line change in `plan.ts`.
3. Re-ran the same test file — 45/45 pass (green).

## Scope discipline

Per the task's explicit constraints:
- Only the `next-id` subcommand is pre-approved (prefix form
  `Bash(cairn task next-id:*)`), matching the pattern task #80 established
  for the mutating-subcommand denies in `src/claude-settings.ts`.
- No other `cairn task` subcommand, no git rules, and no other widening of
  the planner's tool grants were added.
- `cairn.json` was **not** modified (still pinned to the throwaway
  `/tmp/cairn-healthcheck` outfile per the self-modifying-round pin/unpin
  procedure — confirmed before running the health check).
- `src/claude-settings.ts` (task #80's shared allow/deny builders for `cairn
  init`'s `.claude/settings.local.json`) was intentionally left untouched —
  this task is scoped to the planner's own `--allowedTools` flag in
  `plan.ts`, a separate mechanism from the settings-file rules `cairn init`
  writes into a *target* project. The two lists happen to encode the same
  next-id/mutating-subcommand distinction but live in different files for
  different consumers.

## Why deny-vs-allow ordering isn't a concern here

`--allowedTools` on the interactive `claude` planning session is a flat
allowlist, not layered with a deny list the way `cairn init`'s generated
`.claude/settings.local.json` is (per task #80's notes, deny beats allow
there). This flag has no corresponding deny entries, so there's no ordering
hazard to reason about — the note about `next-id` staying out of task #80's
denies is about the *other* mechanism, referenced here only as prior art for
the naming convention (`Bash(cairn task next-id:*)`) and scope discipline.

## Verification

- `bun test test/commands/plan.test.ts` → 45 pass, 0 fail (was 44 before the
  new test was added; net +1 test, and the pre-existing exact-string test
  was updated in place rather than duplicated).
- `bun run test` → **880 pass, 0 fail** across 30 files (was 879 before).
- Health check `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile
  /tmp/cairn-healthcheck` → clean (confirmed `cairn.json` still points at the
  throwaway outfile before running, per the pinned-round procedure; did not
  modify `cairn.json`).
- Grepped for other references to the old literal `Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent`
  string: only match outside `plan.ts`/tests is `.cairn/planning-notes.md:15`,
  a historical planning-discussion doc (not source, not in this task's file
  scope) — left untouched.

## Nothing left for the next agent on this task

The change is a single flag-string addition plus its test; no follow-on work
or discovered gaps.

tasks.title: Mark planner, audit-planner and summarizer as internal agents
tasks.description:
`buildSystemPrompt` (src/commands/run.ts, around lines 63-86) injects an assigned specialist agent's file body verbatim into the executor's system prompt under the heading "SPECIALIST INSTRUCTIONS: You have been assigned as a specialist agent for this task. Follow these instructions in addition to your standard workflow."

It already guards against misuse: at around line 68, if the agent is marked `internal: true` it warns and falls back to the generalist prompt. But ONLY `agents/post-task-reviewer.md` carries that flag. `agents/planner.md`, `agents/audit-planner.md`, and `agents/summarizer.md` have NO frontmatter at all, so the guard never fires for them.

This is not hypothetical. Tasks #70 and #71 in the previous round both ran with `agent: planner`. Injecting `planner.md`'s body into an executor tells it to "Have a conversation with the user about what they want to accomplish", to "Focus on understanding and planning, not implementation details", and — worst — "ONLY write to planning-notes.md — do NOT write tasks.json or modify any other files". None of that is appropriate for a headless `claude -p` implementation agent, and there is no user present to converse with.

Add YAML frontmatter with `name`, `description`, and `internal: true` to all three files, matching the format already used in `agents/post-task-reviewer.md`.

VERIFY TWO THINGS before finishing:
1. That agent discovery actually parses the flag into `AgentInfo.internal` (see `src/types.ts` and the discovery helper) so the run.ts guard fires. Add or extend a test covering it.
2. That adding frontmatter does not break `buildAgentArgs` (src/agent-prompt.ts), which reads the WHOLE file including frontmatter and passes it as the agent prompt for `cairn plan` and `cairn summarize`. `post-task-reviewer.md` already has frontmatter and works this way, so there is precedent — confirm, do not assume.

Also confirm these three still appear in the `cairn plan` preflight's specialist listing where appropriate — `buildDynamicContext` in src/commands/plan.ts filters on `!a.internal`, so this change WILL remove them from that list. That is correct and intended (they are not executor specialists), but note it in your task notes.

Propagation: these are the bundled source files; each project's `.claude/agents/` copies refresh when `cairn init` is re-run. Do not edit `.claude/agents/*.md` directly.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.

tasks.title: CLAUDE.md — truth-up the tasks.json enforcement story
tasks.description:
Two corrections to `CLAUDE.md`'s "Agent workflow" section.

1. THE ENFORCEMENT SET IS NOW WRONG. CLAUDE.md says direct `Edit`/`Write` on `tasks.json` is "enforced two ways: the per-agent system prompt explicitly bans it, and the post-task reviewer runs with a directory-scoped allowlist covering only `<dataDir>/reviews/**`". There was an unstated THIRD lock: the reviewer had no Bash at all, so it could not run `cairn task set-status` either. Task #77 removes that lock by granting the reviewer git-inspection subcommands and the reviewed task's test commands.

   Document the actual enforcement set as it now stands: the prompt ban, the directory-scoped write allowlist, and the explicit `permissions.deny` rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands that `cairn init` writes (task #80). Record two facts that are easy to get wrong:
   - Deny rules are NOT enforced under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so they do not bind `cairn run` execution agents. They bind the reviewer and planner, which run in normal permission mode. This asymmetry is intended.
   - The deny covers mutating subcommands ONLY. A blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)` would break `cairn task next-id`, which task generation requires; deny beats allow with no exception mechanism.

2. SCOPE THE BAN ITSELF. "Direct `Edit` or `Write` on `tasks.json` is forbidden" currently contradicts `commands/generate-tasks.md:159`, which explicitly instructs the planning session to write `.cairn/tasks.json` using the Write tool. Both are right in intent — the ban targets EXECUTION AGENTS mutating a live task list mid-round, whereas task generation authors the file wholesale between rounds. Add a clause saying so, so the two documents stop contradicting each other.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is currently pinned to a throwaway outfile (`bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`) and is USER-MANAGED for this round. CLAUDE.md documents the REAL value (`bun run build` / `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile dist/cairn`) and must continue to. While the round runs, CLAUDE.md and `cairn.json` will legitimately disagree about the health check. That disagreement is EXPECTED and must NOT be "fixed" in either direction. In a previous round exactly this trap caused the pinned value to be committed permanently.

tasks.title: README.md — document the permission rules init now writes
tasks.description:
Document the new `cairn init` behavior added in task #80.

Add to `README.md` — the Workflow > Initialize section is the natural home, with a cross-reference from Configuration if useful:

1. That `cairn init` offers to write permission rules to `.claude/settings.local.json`, and that the prompt defaults to yes but is skippable.
2. WHAT gets written: read-only git inspection subcommands, allow rules derived from the project's `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand`, and deny rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands.
3. WHY: agents that verify a task actually landed — chiefly the post-task reviewer — need to run tests and inspect history. Without these rules a fresh project denies them outright in headless mode.
4. That EXISTING settings are MERGED, not replaced: `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` are unioned and every other key is preserved untouched. A user who already has settings from plain `claude` usage will not lose them.
5. That the user should add `.claude/settings.local.json` to their own gitignore — Cairn deliberately does not edit `.gitignore` or global git config, and Claude Code only auto-ignores that file when it writes the file itself.

Keep the existing README structure and table formatting conventions.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is pinned to a throwaway outfile and is user-managed for this round. Any disagreement between documentation and `cairn.json`'s current value is EXPECTED — do not reconcile it.
